title: Fatal dengue cases in travellers from 1995 to 2025: A targeted review.

analysis.scope_and_question: Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease endemic in 136 countries and territories, with over 14 million cases and more than 10,000 deaths reported globally in 2024 alone. PubMed searches using terms related to dengue, mortality, and travel were complemented by hand-searching conference proceedings, national and international surveillance reports, publicly accessible national infectious disease databases, media reports, and anecdotal notifications. Data were extracted, cross-referenced to avoid duplication, and analysed descriptively.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Sixty-seven fatal travel-related dengue cases were identified, of which 55 were classified as confirmed/probable and 12 cases had limited information. Confirmed/probable fatal cases occurred among patients aged <1-79 years; 25.5% were female, 21.8% were male, and in 52.7% sex was not documented. Where infection status was available, most were primary infections (9/16). Reported fatal manifestations included neurological, cardiac, haemorrhagic, and hyperinflammatory complications. Dengue-related mortality among travellers is rare but likely under-recognised and underreported.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Diagnostic and reporting heterogeneity was substantial, and surveillance gaps were evident.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Strengthened diagnostic capacity and heightened clinical awareness may support earlier recognition and management of severe cases in travellers, while harmonised international reporting systems could improve case ascertainment and contribute to future prevention strategies.

Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral disease endemic in 136 countries, with over 14 million cases and more than 10,000 deaths reported in 2024. The study identified 67 fatal cases, with 55 classified as confirmed/probable and 12 with limited information. Most confirmed cases were primary infections, and fatal manifestations included neurological, cardiac, haemorrhagic, and hyperinflammatory complications. Despite the rarity of dengue-related mortality in travellers, the review highlights underreporting and under-recognition. The findings suggest the need for improved diagnostic capacity and harmonised international reporting systems to enhance case detection and prevention strategies.

title: Bifurcation analysis and optimal control of a Dengue fever model with saturated nonlinear incidence and dual time delays

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue fever remains a serious public health challenge, and mathematical models offer a valuable lens for understanding its dynamics and guiding control efforts.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study develops and analyses a seven-compartment deterministic model that links human and mosquito populations through coupled transmission pathways.
analysis.methods: The model incorporates several features not previously combined in the dengue literature: a saturated incidence function that captures crowding effects in both transmission directions, two biologically distinct incubation delays representing the time the virus spends in humans and in mosquitoes separately, gradual loss of temporary immunity after recovery, and a three-component optimal control framework.
analysis.main_results: The threshold quantity governing outbreak potential is derived and estimated at approximately 2.37 under baseline conditions. When this threshold falls to or below one, the disease-free equilibrium is shown to be globally asymptotically stable; when it exceeds one, a unique endemic equilibrium emerges; its local asymptotic stability is established analytically for the full DDE model, and global stability is proved for the limiting ODE case (no delays, no saturation, no waning immunity).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A notable finding is that the system can sustain endemic transmission even when the threshold is driven below one, provided that the saturation constant satisfies α > α † and the waning immunity rate δ h > 0 act together—a result with direct implications for eradication strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Analysis of the incubation delay reveals that beyond a critical value of roughly 9.4 days, the system transitions into sustained oscillations, offering a mechanistic explanation for the seasonal cycles commonly observed in Southeast Asian dengue data.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Sensitivity analysis highlights mosquito mortality as the most influential parameter. Numerical simulations validate all theoretical results.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a mathematical model of dengue fever that incorporates a saturated nonlinear incidence function, dual time delays for human and mosquito incubation, and waning immunity. The model derives a threshold quantity for outbreak potential, estimated at 2.37 under baseline conditions. It demonstrates that disease-free equilibrium is globally stable when the threshold is below one, while an endemic equilibrium emerges when it exceeds one. The model also reveals that sustained oscillations can occur beyond a critical incubation delay of 9.4 days, potentially explaining seasonal dengue patterns. The findings suggest that combined intervention strategies are more effective than single measures for disease control. Sensitivity analysis identifies mosquito mortality as the most influential parameter, and numerical simulations confirm the theoretical results. The study contributes to understanding dengue dynamics and informs public health strategies for control and eradication.

title: Adult Immunogenicity and Descriptive Safety of TAK-003 Dengue Vaccination: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Adult TAK-003 data differ by formulation, baseline dengue status, coadministration, and outcome definition. To synthesize adult immunogenicity and safety of the licensed two-dose final formulation of TAK-003.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We searched PubMed, Scopus, CENTRAL-derived records, registries, regulatory sources, and citations to the final search update. Screening, extraction, appraisal, and analysis used a reproducible computational workflow without independent duplicate verification. Seropositivity and 270-day serious adverse event (SAE) risk were modeled with binomial-normal logit models; comparative reactogenicity used random-effects risk ratios with modified Hartung-Knapp intervals.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among 620 baseline-seronegative adults, pooled seropositivity about 30 days after dose 2 was 98.7% for DENV-1 (95% CI 95.8–99.6), 99.0% for DENV-2 (97.9–99.6), 96.9% for DENV-3 (95.2–98.0), and 98.4% for DENV-4 (97.0–99.1). With DEN307 added, estimates were 98.8%, 99.2%, 97.1%, and 98.5% (752 participants per serotype). Final-formulation TAK-003 gave high short-term seropositivity in selected adult trial populations.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Certainty was low or very low, and inference is limited by study size, surrogate outcomes, and uncontrolled safety data. Across four cohorts, 29/1,468 participants had an SAE through day 270 (pooled risk 2.0%, 95% CI 1.4–2.8). Pain and headache estimates, each from two studies, were highly imprecise.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The SAE risk was uncontrolled and does not establish comparative safety.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize the immunogenicity and safety of the licensed two-dose final formulation of TAK-003 in adults. The review included 5 trials with quantitative outcomes, focusing on seropositivity and serious adverse events (SAEs). Among baseline-seronegative adults, pooled seropositivity was high for all four dengue serotypes, with estimates ranging from 96.9% to 99.0%. However, the SAE risk was uncontrolled, and the certainty of evidence was low or very low due to study size, surrogate outcomes, and lack of safety data control. Pain and headache estimates were imprecise. The findings suggest that TAK-003 has strong immunogenicity in selected adult populations but highlight the need for further research to address safety concerns and improve precision in reactogenicity assessments.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of the AST-to-Platelet Ratio Index (APRI) for severe or complicated dengue: a systematic review and meta-analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of APRI for identifying severe or complicated dengue, according to the target-condition definitions used in the included studies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Seven electronic databases were searched from inception to March 13, 2026. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies guidance. Pooled estimates were obtained using a frequentist bivariate random-effects Reitsma model fitted by restricted maximum likelihood estimation. Heterogeneity, threshold effects and sensitivity analyses were assessed. A separate sensitivity analysis was restricted to studies comparing severe with non-severe dengue.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Eight studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, of which six comprising 948 participants were quantitatively pooled. Pooled sensitivity was 0.75 (95% confidence interval: 0.66–0.82), and pooled specificity was 0.80 (95% confidence interval: 0.76–0.84). The positive likelihood ratio was 3.76, the negative likelihood ratio was 0.32 and the diagnostic odds ratio was 12.42. The area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.841. Leave-one-out analyses produced similar estimates. The review also examined methodological limitations affecting the interpretation and potential clinical applicability of the findings.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Variation in target-condition definitions and the wide range of retrospectively selected APRI thresholds limit clinical applicability, while retrospective threshold selection may overestimate diagnostic performance. The pooled estimates should not be interpreted as applying exclusively to strictly defined severe dengue.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prospective validation is required before routine use alongside clinical assessment and serial laboratory monitoring.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis assessed the diagnostic accuracy of the AST-to-Platelet Ratio Index (APRI) for severe or complicated dengue. Seven electronic databases were searched up to March 13, 2026, and eight studies were included, with six providing quantitative data. Pooled sensitivity was 0.75 (95% CI: 0.66–0.82), and pooled specificity was 0.80 (95% CI: 0.76–0.84). The positive likelihood ratio was 3.76, the negative likelihood ratio was 0.32, and the diagnostic odds ratio was 12.42. The area under the summary receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.841. However, the review highlighted limitations, including variation in target-condition definitions and retrospective threshold selection, which may overestimate diagnostic performance. Prospective validation is recommended for routine clinical use of APRI.

analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized Hepatitis C virus (HCV) and dengue virus (DENV) as complementary models to evaluate the role of reticulon-3 (RTN3) in viral replication and extracellular-vesicle-mediated transfer, despite their distinct transmission routes, tissue tropisms, and disease courses.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that RTN3 plays a functional role in vesicle-associated output for HCV and DENV, but its involvement is not universal across all RNA viruses, and the precise mechanism of cargo selection is not yet established.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that understanding RTN3's role in viral replication and dissemination could inform the development of broad-spectrum antiviral interventions targeting host-virus interactions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of reticulon-3 (RTN3) in the replication and dissemination of dengue virus (DENV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV). The study suggests that RTN3 may play a functional role in this process for DENV and HCV, though its involvement is not universal. These findings could inform the development of antiviral strategies targeting host-virus interactions, but the evidence is limited by the unresolved mechanisms and the lack of direct confirmation of RTN3's role in viral RNA recognition and incorporation. The study's results are based on abstract-only evidence, and the confidence in these findings is moderate due to the absence of detailed experimental data.

title: Dengue fever in Iran: epidemiology, vectors, diagnostics, and public health challenges: a comprehensive systematic literature review (2020–2026)

analysis.scope_and_question: Dengue fever has transitioned from an occasional imported infection to a growing domestic public health concern in Iran. The review focuses on the epidemiology, vectors, diagnostics, and public health challenges associated with dengue virus in Iran.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic literature review, conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines (with acknowledged deviations), analyzed 46 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026. A limited, exploratory meta-analysis of seroprevalence estimates from a subset of comparable studies (five estimates from three primary studies, of which only three were directly observed seroprevalence measurements) yielded a pooled national estimate of 3.96% [95% CI: 1.20–6.72], with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 98.5%, p < 0.01).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The critical outbreak in Sistan and Baluchestan Province in 2024, involving 1,057 confirmed cases (80.7% locally transmitted), suggests a threat of endemic establishment rather than having reached endemicity. The review identifies critical gaps in surveillance infrastructure, molecular diagnostic capacity, and healthcare system preparedness.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Publication bias analyses (funnel plot asymmetry; Egger’s test: p = 0.028) suggested potential underrepresentation of low-prevalence regions, but these findings are unreliable with few studies and should be interpreted with extreme caution. The review also highlights the need for more comprehensive data on dengue virus transmission dynamics and vector behavior.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Key recommendations include implementing integrated surveillance systems, adopting genomic epidemiology, and enhancing regional collaboration. Without immediate and coordinated action, Iran faces an imminent risk of transitioning to endemic dengue transmission.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic literature review examines the growing public health concern of dengue fever in Iran, focusing on its epidemiology, vectors, diagnostics, and challenges. The review analyzed 46 studies published between 2020 and 2026, with a meta-analysis of seroprevalence estimates showing a pooled national estimate of 3.96% [95% CI: 1.20–6.72], though substantial heterogeneity was noted. A critical outbreak in 2024, with 80.7% locally transmitted cases, indicates a potential shift toward endemicity. The review highlights gaps in surveillance, diagnostics, and healthcare preparedness, and recommends integrated systems, genomic epidemiology, and regional collaboration. Publication bias analyses suggest caution in interpreting findings due to limited data. Immediate action is needed to prevent the transition to endemic dengue transmission in Iran.

title: Effect of Carica papaya Leaf Extract on Platelet Count in Dengue-Induced Thrombocytopenia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis

analysis.scope_and_question: Dengue fever remains a prime public health trouble in tropical regions and is regularly related to thrombocytopenia. The review focuses on the effect of Carica papaya leaf extract (CPLE) on platelet count in dengue-induced thrombocytopenia.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This systematic overview was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) Guidelines. The Cochrane Risk of Bias tool (RoB 2.0) and the ROBINS-I tool (Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions) were used to evaluate bias, and Rstudio was used for statistical analysis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Numerous studies have analyzed the ability of Carica papaya leaves, which have verified effective as a therapy for thrombocytopenia. Carica papaya leaf extract confirmed a significant increase in platelet count compared to the control (SMD = 0.40; 95% CI: 0.18–0.63; p = 0.0003).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Subgroup analysis by day confirmed that the impact was not extensive on days 2 and 4, but significant on days 3 (SMD = 0.46; 95% CI: 0.04–0.87) and 5 (SMD = 0.63; 95% CI: 0.14–1.13), without a significant difference among the assessment times. Within the adult population (29 studies; n = 4,133), the intervention had a significant effect (SMD = 0.52; 95% CI: 0.31–0.73; p < 0.0001) with an increasing effect from day 3 to 5. Within the pediatric population (7 studies; n = 1,260), the intervention impact varied over time, with a non-significant effect on day 2, a significant effect on day 3 (SMD = 0.54; 95% CI: 0.31–0.77), and day 5 (SMD = 1.21; 95% CI: 0.96–1.45), and a significant difference among evaluation days (p < 0.0001).
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Carica papaya leaf extract adjunctive therapy effectively increases platelets in dengue patients with thrombocytopenia in the adult population, but not significantly in children.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the effect of Carica papaya leaf extract on platelet count in dengue-induced thrombocytopenia. The extract was found to significantly increase platelet counts, with more pronounced effects in adults compared to children.

title: Serum Cortisol and Lipid Profile as Predictors of Dengue Severity in Children: A Prospective Observational Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Early prediction of severe dengue in children continues to be difficult, even with World Health Organisation (WHO) warning signs. Serum cortisol and lipid profile are routinely available laboratory parameters and may provide additional information regarding disease severity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective observational study was conducted in the Department of Paediatrics, SRM Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, Kattankulathur, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India, over two years (July 2024-July 2026). A total of 90 dengue NS1 or IgM ELISA-positive children aged between 0-14 years with warning signs and presenting between days 3 and 7 of illness were enrolled after informed consent.
analysis.methods: Serum cortisol and fasting lipid profile were measured at enrolment, and the day of illness at sampling was recorded. Categorical variables were compared using the Chisquare test and continuous variables using the independent-samples t-test; p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant.
analysis.main_results: In the present study, 15 out of 90 (16.67%) children progressed to severe dengue. Fluid accumulation, mucosal bleeding, lethargy, and significant liver enlargement were significantly associated with progression to severe dengue. Severe dengue was also associated with higher total leucocyte count and serum urea, lower serum sodium and bicarbonate, and prolonged prothrombin time. Mean serum cortisol was higher in children who progressed to severe dengue than in those who did not (18.74±6.14 vs 15.46±4.48 μg/dL; p-value =0.017). Mean triglyceride levels were also higher (220.07±141.71 vs 162.97±62.69 mg/dL; p-value =0.014), whereas mean total cholesterol levels were lower (99.67±23.70 vs 122.01±26.71 mg/dL; p-value =0.003).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: High levels of cortisol and triglycerides with low levels of total cholesterol at the time of admission are strongly linked to the development of severe dengue.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings may inform the development of non-invasive biomarkers for early identification of children at risk of severe dengue, aiding in targeted clinical management and resource allocation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of statistical tests and a defined cohort.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate the significance of serum cortisol and lipid profile in forecasting the advancement to severe dengue in children. Conducted over two years in a paediatric department in India, it enrolled 90 dengue-positive children with warning signs. Results showed that 16.67% of children progressed to severe dengue, with higher cortisol and triglyceride levels and lower total cholesterol levels associated with this progression. The authors concluded that these biomarkers may be useful in predicting severe dengue. However, the study's observational design and potential confounding factors limit the confidence in the findings, which are considered moderate in strength.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to describe the clinical and laboratory profiles of pediatric patients with dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) at Prof. Kandou General Hospital during the period January 2023–December 2024.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a retrospective and descriptive study using patient medical records from 2023 to 2024. The majority of patients were from Manado City and in good nutritional status.
analysis.methods: This study used patient medical records as data sources. It was a retrospective and descriptive study design.
analysis.main_results: The results showed that most cases occurred in 2024, with the largest age group being 6–12 years old and predominantly male. Laboratory findings showed leukopenia (45% of patients), increased hematocrit (53.9%), and severe thrombocytopenia (66.3%).

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the clinical and laboratory profiles of pediatric patients with dengue hemorrhagic fever (DHF) at Prof. Dr. R. D. Kandou General Hospital from January 2023 to December 2024. It is a retrospective descriptive study using patient medical records. The results indicate that most cases occurred in 2024, predominantly in male children aged 6–12 years. Laboratory findings revealed leukopenia in 45% of patients, increased hematocrit in 53.9%, and severe thrombocytopenia in 66.3%. The most common DHF category was Grade 3 (64.1%), and the mortality rate was 2.9%. The study highlights the importance of early detection and optimal management during critical phases of the disease. However, the reliance on medical records may introduce limitations in data accuracy and completeness.

title: Integrating community participation with a weighted dengue risk-stratification framework for commune-level prioritization in Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province, Vietnam

analysis.research_question_and_background: Dengue prevention programs require transparent commune-level prioritization when epidemiological, entomological, and operational information must be combined.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We implemented a stakeholder-informed weighted dengue risk-stratification framework in 72 communes, wards, and towns in Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province, Vietnam.
analysis.methods: Community participatory action research (CPAR) provided the participatory implementation approach, whereas the quantitative procedure was a deterministic additive score implemented in MS Access.
analysis.main_results: The 2022 score was inversely associated with absolute 2022 incidence (Spearman rho = -0.304, p = 0.009), with poor discrimination for upper-quartile absolute incidence (AUC = 0.335).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: High-priority units showed a larger relative increase from their 2016–2020 mean than intermediate-priority units (median 5.36-fold vs. 2.23-fold; p = 0.001), with an exploratory AUC of 0.711 for upper-quartile relative rebound.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The framework should be interpreted as a transparent local prioritization tool rather than a probabilistic prediction model.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Classifications were sensitive to cut-offs and one-level uncertainty in ordinal inputs. Prospective multi-year and external validation, assessor-reliability evaluation, and dengue-specific recalibration are required before broader use.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a transparent commune-level prioritization framework for dengue prevention programs by integrating epidemiological, entomological, and operational data. The framework was implemented in 72 communes, wards, and towns in Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province, Vietnam, using a deterministic additive score in MS Access. The January 2022 score was evaluated against observed 2022 incidence, revealing an inverse association with absolute incidence (Spearman rho = -0.304, p = 0.009) and poor discrimination for upper-quartile absolute incidence (AUC = 0.335). High-priority units showed a larger relative increase in incidence compared to intermediate-priority units (median 5.36-fold vs. 2.23-fold; p = 0.001), with an exploratory AUC of 0.711 for upper-quartile relative rebound. The framework was described as a transparent local prioritization tool rather than a probabilistic prediction model. However, the study noted that classifications were sensitive to cut-offs and uncertainty in ordinal inputs, and emphasized the need for prospective multi-year validation, assessor-reliability evaluation, and dengue-specific recalibration before broader use.

title: Spontaneous Splenic Rupture During the Recovery Phase of Severe Dengue Fever: Perioperative Anaesthetic Management of an Emergency Splenectomy

analysis.research_question_and_background: Spontaneous splenic rupture is a rare but life-threatening complication of dengue fever, most commonly reported during the critical phase. This case highlights an unusual occurrence during the recovery phase.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes an emergency splenectomy performed on a 35-year-old previously healthy man with severe dengue fever who developed spontaneous splenic rupture during the recovery phase.
analysis.methods: Contrast-enhanced computed tomography was used to confirm splenic rupture with haemoperitoneum, and rotational thromboelastometry-guided transfusion supported targeted blood product therapy during the perioperative management.
analysis.main_results: The patient developed sudden left upper quadrant pain, hypotension, tachycardia, and anaemia, which were consistent with splenic rupture. Histopathology confirmed extensive intraparenchymal haemorrhage and capsular disruption.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret this case as an example of spontaneous splenic rupture occurring during the recovery phase of dengue fever, which is not typically reported in the literature.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This case provides important insights into the potential for splenic rupture during the recovery phase of dengue fever, emphasizing the need for vigilance in clinical management.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a single case report, which limits its generalizability. However, the findings are supported by direct clinical and histopathological evidence, providing a moderate level of confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a rare and life-threatening complication of dengue fever, spontaneous splenic rupture, occurring during the recovery phase rather than the critical phase. The patient, a 35-year-old previously healthy man with severe dengue, developed sudden left upper quadrant pain, hypotension, tachycardia, and anaemia. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography confirmed splenic rupture with haemoperitoneum, and emergency splenectomy was performed under general anaesthesia. Rotational thromboelastometry-guided transfusion supported targeted blood product therapy. Histopathology confirmed extensive intraparenchymal haemorrhage and capsular disruption. The patient recovered well and was discharged in a stable condition. This case highlights the need to consider splenic rupture even during the recovery phase of dengue fever and the importance of early diagnosis, prompt surgery, and meticulous perioperative management. The study is a single case report, which limits its generalizability, but the findings are supported by direct clinical and histopathological evidence, providing a moderate level of confidence.

title: A standardized mosquito-to-mouse transmission assay with spatially defined bite areas

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a method for investigating early tissue-level events following vector-mediated transmission of dengue virus, as mosquito-borne viruses initiate infection in the skin where interactions between viral particles, host cells, and mosquito saliva can influence early infection and subsequent viral dissemination.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a standardized mosquito-to-mouse transmission assay designed to investigate early tissue-level events during dengue virus transmission. The method uses a 3D-printed feeding device, individual mosquito exposure, and perforated adhesive tape to define and mark biting areas. The protocol was demonstrated using Dengue virus (DENV)-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes and C57BL/6J mice. The study highlights the utility of this method for understanding dengue virus dissemination and its potential adaptation for other vector-pathogen systems. The evidence is based on a single experiment with DENV, and no limitations are reported.

title: Stakeholder digital readiness for AI-driven dengue surveillance and reporting system

analysis.research_question_and_background: As the public health sector moves towards digital health transformation, artificial intelligence offers opportunities to improve disease surveillance, early disease detection and strengthen reporting systems. However, the adoption of these technologies depends on stakeholder knowledge, readiness, and practices.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study employed a cross-sectional quantitative mixed-mode survey. The questionnaire comprised of multiple choice and open-ended questions with 397 participants and 391 eligible data registrations. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Study participants exhibited strong digital infrastructure readiness and substantial adoption willingness to AI-driven eHealth solutions. The most desired AI feature is patient engagement chatbots at 86.3%.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study design or evidence strength assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines stakeholder digital readiness for AI-driven dengue surveillance and reporting systems in Kingston, Jamaica. It highlights the high level of readiness and willingness to adopt AI tools among participants, with 72.1% reporting high readiness and 86.3% expressing interest in patient engagement chatbots. The research underscores the importance of integrating community-based knowledge and technology readiness in public health initiatives. However, the study does not explicitly report limitations or evidence strength assessment. The findings suggest that while there is strong potential for AI integration, concerns about data privacy and trust in the system persist.

title: Malaria and Dengue Co-infection in Pregnancy Causing Severe Thrombocytopenia: A Case Report Highlighting Diagnostic and Management Challenges Due to Overlapping Clinical Features

analysis.research_question_and_background: Malaria and dengue are mosquito-borne infections that pose significant health risks during pregnancy and may adversely affect maternal and fetal outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes a 22-year-old primigravida at 37 weeks and 4 days of gestation who presented with headache, fever, vomiting and diarrhoea, and was diagnosed with malaria and dengue coinfection.
analysis.methods: Testing identified Plasmodium vivax malaria, and dengue-specific IgM and IgG antibodies were positive. Management included intravenous crystalloid fluids, platelet transfusions, fresh frozen plasma and chloroquine.
analysis.main_results: The platelet count was 40,000/μL at the receiving hospital, and ultrasound showed oligohydramnios with an amniotic fluid index of 4.14 cm. The platelet count improved to 60,000/μL on the third day, and to 128,000/μL on the seventh day. She was discharged on the twelfth day.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that pregnant women diagnosed with either infection who exhibit severe symptoms should be extensively investigated for coinfection, and prompt treatment should be initiated to optimise maternal and fetal outcomes.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of extensive targeted testing and prompt treatment for coinfection in pregnant women to minimise adverse obstetric outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a case report, which limits its generalisability, but the evidence is strong due to the detailed clinical presentation and management.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 22-year-old pregnant woman who presented with severe symptoms and was diagnosed with malaria and dengue coinfection. The overlapping clinical features of these infections complicated diagnosis and necessitated prompt management. The patient's platelet count was severely reduced, and ultrasound findings indicated oligohydramnios. Management included intravenous fluids, platelet transfusions, and antimalarial treatment. The platelet count improved over the course of the hospital stay, and the patient was discharged without reported complications. The authors highlight the importance of extensive testing and timely treatment for coinfection in pregnant women to optimise maternal and fetal outcomes. The study's limitations include its case report design, which restricts generalisability, but the evidence is strong due to the detailed clinical and laboratory findings.

title: Impact of a point-of-care rapid diagnostic test on the dengue diagnostic cascade in an emergency department in a non-endemic setting: A before-after study (RaDDEO).

analysis.research_question_and_background: Timely recognition of dengue is increasingly important in non-endemic regions, where imported viremic cases may trigger local transmission. We evaluated whether introducing a combined point-of-care rapid diagnostic test (RDT; NS1/IgM/IgG) shortened the time to dengue diagnosis in an emergency department.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Single-center retrospective before-after study in Montpellier University Hospital, southern France. Adults undergoing dengue testing were compared between pre-RDT (10/2022-07/2024) and post-RDT (08/2024-05/2026) periods.
analysis.methods: The primary endpoint was the time from arrival to availability of the diagnostic result. RDT performance was assessed against the clinical diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: Among 88 patients (36 pre-, 52 post-RDT), 28 had dengue, all of them returning travelers, and 57% had sought healthcare before ED presentation. After RDT implementation, time to diagnosis decreased from 24.3 to 2.5 h (median gain 19.6 h, 95%CI 13.9-44.8; p < 0.001). The most time-consuming step was laboratory turnaround (median 25.6 h). While no significant differences were observed in terms of length of stay, hospital admission, and mandatory notification, the study was underpowered to assess these outcomes. RDT sensitivity was 100% and specificity 70.3%; all false positives were antibody bands, primarily in patients with imported malaria.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The RDT shortened time to diagnosis by 20 h without missing any cases of acute dengue.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the potential of point-of-care RDTs to improve diagnostic efficiency in non-endemic settings, which could aid in early intervention and prevention of local transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was underpowered to assess outcomes such as length of stay, hospital admission, and mandatory notification, and the evidence strength is moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the impact of introducing a combined point-of-care rapid diagnostic test (RDT) for dengue in an emergency department in a non-endemic setting. The RDT significantly reduced the time to diagnosis from 24.3 to 2.5 hours, with a median gain of 19.6 hours. However, it did not accelerate downstream clinical or public-health processes, and the study was underpowered to assess these outcomes. The RDT demonstrated 100% sensitivity and 70.3% specificity, with false positives primarily due to antibody bands in patients with imported malaria. These results suggest that RDTs can enhance diagnostic efficiency in non-endemic regions, but further research is needed to evaluate their broader impact on clinical and public health outcomes.

title: Aedes larval breeding sites in public places and their spatial overlay with reported dengue cases in Pedurungan, Semarang, Indonesia

analysis.methods: The study used a single-larva method to survey public places and adapted house-based indices (HI, CI, BI, LFI) to public settings. A descriptive GIS overlay was employed to map reported dengue cases with larval breeding sites.
analysis.main_results: Thirty public places (30.93%) and 75 of 389 containers (19.28%) were larva-positive. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights the importance of public places as potential breeding sites for Aedes mosquitoes, which are vectors for dengue virus. It provides a novel spatial analysis of dengue cases in relation to these sites.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that public places should be included in dengue surveillance efforts, as they may contribute significantly to mosquito breeding and transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's sample is not representative due to prioritization of sites near reported cases, and no clear graded pattern was observed in cumulative incidence across categories. The evidence is moderate in strength.

analysis.study_design_and_population: This research uses a correlational method with a cross-sectional approach and a sampling technique using purposive sampling. The sample in this study consisted of 85 respondents.
analysis.methods: The research instrument used was a questionnaire developed from (Indonesian Ministry of Health, 2018) in the journal Lahagu et al., 2021. Data analysis techniques use univariate and bivariate analysis.
analysis.main_results: Statistical research results using the chi-square test showed that there was a relationship between the level of knowledge of inpatients' families and the incidence of dengue hemorrhagic fever at Vita Insani Hospital, Pematangsiantar with a value of p = 0.003 (p > 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating a relationship between family knowledge levels and dengue hemorrhagic fever incidence, which is a novel observation in the context of hospital-based family awareness programs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of targeted family education programs to reduce the incidence of dengue hemorrhagic fever in hospital settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's evidence is limited by its cross-sectional design and small sample size, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence strength is moderate.

The study suggests that improving family knowledge could be a strategy to reduce the incidence of dengue hemorrhagic fever in hospital settings. However, the findings are limited by the study's design and small sample size, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study does not provide detailed mechanisms or causal explanations.

title: Prevenção da dengue em jogo

analysis.research_question_and_background: A prevenção da dengue requer a participação da população na identificação e eliminação de situações que favorecem a reprodução do Aedes aegypti, tornando a educação em saúde um componente relevante das estratégias de enfrentamento das arboviroses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: O objetivo deste trabalho é relatar uma experiência educativa voltada à prevenção da dengue, desenvolvida por meio de uma dinâmica baseada em jogo de associação durante o evento “Conhecendo a UNIPAMPA”, realizado em 11 de setembro de 2026, na Universidade Federal do Pampa (UNIPAMPA), Campus Uruguaiana.
analysis.methods: Para a atividade, utilizou-se o “Dominó da Dengue”, composto por peças que estabelecem associações entre perguntas e respostas relacionadas à transmissão da doença, ao reconhecimento de sinais e sintomas e, principalmente, às medidas de prevenção.
analysis.main_results: Observou-se dificuldade recorrente na identificação do mosquito transmissor: alguns estudantes respondiam apenas “mosquito” ou escolhiam uma resposta ao acaso. Apesar dessa dificuldade, de modo geral, os alunos conseguiam concluir o jogo com relativa facilidade.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: A dinâmica de associação favoreceu a participação e possibilitou momentos de diálogo durante a atividade, permitindo que o jogo funcionasse como mediador da discussão sobre comportamentos individuais e coletivos relacionados à prevenção.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: A experiência possibilitou trabalhar medidas preventivas a partir de situações concretas e estimular o reconhecimento da responsabilidade compartilhada no controle do Aedes aegypti.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: A ação integrou as atividades do Grupo 5 – Comunicação e Inovação do Programa de Educação pelo Trabalho para a Saúde (PET-Saúde) – Clima.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports on an educational initiative aimed at preventing dengue through an interactive game-based approach during the event 'Conhecendo a UNIPAMPA' on September 11, 2026, at the Federal University of Pampa (UNIPAMPA) in Uruguaiana. The game, called 'Dominó da Dengue', was designed to foster associations between questions and answers related to dengue transmission, symptoms, and prevention measures. The study involved students from the final years of elementary and high school, distributed across multiple classes without a reported total number of participants. The main results indicated that while students faced challenges in identifying the Aedes aegypti mosquito, they generally completed the game with relative ease. The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the potential of ludic strategies to promote participatory approaches in public health education, encouraging dialogue on individual and collective behaviors related to dengue prevention. The study highlights the importance of integrating practical knowledge into health education to enhance community engagement. However, the lack of a specified sample size and the absence of quantitative outcomes limit the strength of the evidence.
